subject: botany
question_text: Distinguish between asexual and sexual reproduction. Why is vegetative reproduction also considered a type of asexual reproduction?

verification.note: Chapter 6 is sourced from the Junior Fastrack botany guide (book p.15), which prints the question and a model answer but NO star ranks and NO year citations. Only ONE source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely pending. The 1+1+1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The book prints the question with a missing question mark ('reproduction Why is …') and non-standard grammar in the table ('capable to produce offsprings'); the card cleans both.

insider_note: Write the distinction as numbered pairs, not prose — examiners tick one mark per contrast row, then look for the vegetative reason as a separate closing sentence.

steps.label: Number of parents
lines: 1) Asexual: a single parent produces the
Sexual: two individuals are involved in
steps.why: The first contrast is the number of individuals involved: one in asexual, two in sexual.
common_mistakes: Writing 'one cell vs two cells' — the contrast is parents (individuals), not cells.
steps.memory_tip: The three rows follow one order: parents (1 vs 2), gametes (none vs fusion), offspring (identical vs different).
steps.margin_note: Write each contrast as a numbered pair of lines.

steps.label: Gamete fusion
lines: 2) Asexual: gametes are not formed and
no fusion of gametes takes place.
Sexual: a male gamete fuses with a
steps.why: This is the defining contrast — the other two rows follow from it: no fusion means one parent is enough and the offspring are identical.
common_mistakes: Writing 'no reproductive cells' — use the word gametes.
steps.memory_tip: No gametes → no mixing → identical offspring. Gametes → mixing → variation. The middle row explains the other two.
steps.margin_note: The word fusion (or syngamy) must appear.

steps.label: Nature of offspring
lines: identical to the parent and to each other
Sexual: offspring are not identical to
the parents or to one another (variation).
steps.why: With no gamete fusion there is no new gene combination, so asexual offspring are exact copies (clones); sexual offspring carry a new combination each time.
common_mistakes: Writing 'similar' for asexual offspring — the point is IDENTICAL (clones).
Not naming variation on the sexual side.
steps.memory_tip: Asexual = an exact copy every time (clone); sexual = a new combination every time (variation).
steps.margin_note: Three contrasts earn 3 marks — one pair of lines each.

steps.label: Why vegetative is asexual

lines.text: One parent + no gamete fusion → asexual

lines: give rise to new plants, with no union
So it is a type of asexual reproduction.
steps.why: The test for asexual reproduction is the two-part check in the box: a single parent and no gamete fusion. Vegetative reproduction satisfies both, so it belongs under asexual reproduction.
common_mistakes: Answering only 'because one parent is involved' — also state that NO gametes fuse.
Calling spore formation vegetative — spores are asexual structures but not vegetative propagules.
steps.memory_tip: Apply the two-part check: one parent? yes. Gamete fusion? no. Both answers place it under asexual.
steps.margin_note: End with the reason sentence — this mark is for the 'why'.
